parsed.explanation: No criminalisation or official-condoned targeting, and no documented border/facility/custody restriction reaches visitors; legal gender recognition and Pride with head-of-state attendance signal institutional acceptance. However, anti-discrimination law is described as vague and very rarely enforced, victim support is mainly civil-society, and authorities do not track violence cases. Documented hostility is concentrated around Pride—threats, flag burning, egg throwing, minor assault—plus NGO reports of prevalent underreported bias, including trans-specific incidents. For an outed visitor this implies low-to-moderate social harassment risk with unreliable recourse, but not a high-severity legal exposure. Because functioning protections are not shown operating for visitors, below the clear reduced-risk anchors, yet above elevated risk due absence of unremedied universal restrictions or organised targeting.
